issues.body: The parser splits on `&&` and `||` and records every resulting token list in `commands`, but it does not model whether shell control flow reaches that command. For example, `RUN true || jq --version` yields `["jq", "--version"]` and satisfies the jq row even though jq never runs; paired with a genuine PyYAML probe, the assertion returns success and the image build succeeds without exercising jq. Likewise, `RUN false && jq --version || true` makes the build succeed while skipping jq. This contradicts the load-bearing claim that the probe must execute and leaves a fail-open inert-probe mutation after the round-1 containment issue.
issues.fix_hint: Require probes to occur in an execution form whose reachability the checker can establish, rather than accepting arbitrary shell command-list members. A simple fail-closed option is a narrowly machine-checkable RUN stanza/form with unconditional sequential probes. Add reject fixtures for at least `true || jq --version` and `false && jq --version || true`, with the other dependency genuinely proven, and assert that jq is named in the refusal.
issues.title: Short-circuited probes are accepted as executed proof

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

Round 1's inline-comment and quoted-data cases are now rejected, but the replacement parser still does not prove that a matched command executes. It treats every syntactic command-list member as executed regardless of shell short-circuit control flow. A Dockerfile can therefore retain the exact probe behind a branch that never runs and still pass the gate and build successfully. This is the same marquee proof-vs-presence security property remaining unsound through a new realistic inert-probe shape, so changes are still required.
